title: The War on Fat: The Seven Countries Study
summary: Josh and Chuck open with a book preorder plug for their upcoming book, then discuss the "war on fat" in the US in the 1980s and 1990s and the Seven Countries Study led by physiologist Ancel Keys, which began in the 1950s and was used to support low-fat dietary guidance and the food pyramid. They cover Keys's background (K rations, Minnesota starvation experiment, Mediterranean diet cookbooks), the six country graph, the choice of seven countries and sixteen cohorts with about 12,763 participants, the findings on serum cholesterol, saturated fat and heart disease (including the Finland, Dalmatia, Crete and Minnesota railroad worker cohorts), later follow-up studies, criticisms of correlation versus causation and the study's design, the sugar and saturated fat finding, the role of processed food and refined sugar, the Dr. Zoe Harcombe critique about sunshine and vitamin D, and modern obesity and diabetes trends. They end with a discussion of alcohol, hangover remedies, and moderation, followed by a listener mail segment about jackhammers and a sign-off.

entities.name: United States Department of Health and Human Services

segments.title: Book preorder announcement
segments.summary: Hosts promote their upcoming first book, Stuff You Should Know: An Incomplete Compendium of Mostly Interesting Things, available for preorder.

segments.title: Opening banter and the war on fat
segments.summary: Hosts introduce the heart healthy episode and argue that fat is not as harmful as the 1980s and 1990s low-fat trend suggested. They say low-fat foods replaced fat with sugar and high fructose corn syrup, which may have contributed to obesity and diabetes.

segments.title: Ancel Keys and the origins of the study
segments.summary: Hosts describe physiologist Ancel Keys, his background including K rations and the Minnesota starvation experiment, his Mediterranean diet books, and his motivation to study heart disease in middle-aged American men.

segments.title: Hypothesis, six country graph and country selection
segments.summary: Keys visited southern Italy in the early 1950s, formed the hypothesis that serum cholesterol and saturated fat drive heart disease, compiled data from 22 countries into the six country graph, and selected seven countries for the study with little funding. The study was designed to run about twenty-five years.

segments.title: Cohorts and the Finland and Dalmatia findings
segments.summary: The study had sixteen cohorts totaling 12,763 men across seven countries. Hosts describe Finland's high-fat diet and heart attack rates, the Dalmatia cohort with low cholesterol and few deaths, and the Crete and Minnesota railroad worker results.

segments.title: Croatia digression and alcohol discussion
segments.summary: Hosts recount a cruise around Italy and the Adriatic, then discuss the wine and chocolate sweet spot, the effects of drinking, and hangover remedies such as B12 shots.

segments.title: Follow-up studies and the sugar finding
segments.summary: Later follow-up studies such as Zutphen and HALE continued the cohorts, finding Mediterranean diet and fish benefits. Reanalysis found sugar correlated with heart disease, but the association disappeared when saturated fat was factored in, suggesting a combined sugar and fat effect with processed food.

segments.title: Criticisms of the Seven Countries Study
segments.summary: Hosts explain criticisms that the study was ecological and correlational, with too many confounding differences between cohorts and no proper control group. They note the Minnesota and Finland comparisons had similar fat intake but different heart attack rates. Zoe Harcombe's point about sunshine and vitamin D is raised.

segments.title: Food pyramid impact and modern health trends
segments.summary: Hosts argue the Department of Health and Human Services ran with the findings and the food pyramid demonized all fats, while good fats from fish, olive oil and avocados are beneficial and industrially processed fats are harmful. They note rising type 2 diabetes and obesity despite the low-fat push.

segments.title: Moderation advice and closing
segments.summary: Hosts advise moderation, portion control and real food, and reflect on their own indulgences before a listener mail segment about jackhammers and a sign-off.

segments.title: Listener mail: jackhammers
segments.summary: A listener named Chris from Massachusetts, a mechanical engineer, writes about the jackhammer episode, explaining the resonant ring of the moil point and his work on dampers. The hosts thank him and invite unsung hero submissions.
